art:main (crates/reflow2-mcp/src/main.rs) REALIZES cap:snapshot-read and cmp:main, and nothing else — so the file that carries the whole CLI surface is traced to one capability it barely touches and NOT to the ones it actually serves. Measured 2026-08-06 by reconcile_artifacts, which returned propagation_seeds ['cap:snapshot-read','cmp:main'] for a change that was entirely about cap:content-store's --content-path argument. CONSEQUENCE: the reconcile-driven path from a code change back to the intent that justified it — the loop link-artifacts step 6 exists to close, and which the skill calls 'the loop the original Reflow never closed' — lands on the wrong capability for any CLI change. The correct blast radius was only obtained because the agent hand-named cap:content-store in add_change_event from judgement; had it trusted the graph, ifc:mcp-tools would never have appeared as a boundary crossing and a tool-surface change would have shipped unnoticed. THE UNDERLYING SHAPE is that main.rs is one atomic artifact standing for many capabilities (content store, HTTP/shared serving, export, import, merge driver, latent mode), which is the pending_expansion case link-artifacts describes: a placeholder standing in for files that should each become their own node, where an atomic registration buys a false tick. Not yet decided whether the fix is more REALIZES edges from the one artifact or a finer artifact decomposition.

═══ SECOND OCCURRENCE, 2026-08-29 — 23 DAYS LATER, SAME COST, SAME WORKAROUND ═══

Surfaced by `unclaimed_findings` during a capture-session pass, as the ONE candidate returned for that session's three ChangeEvents (subjects_examined 13), reached via art:main. Examined and left OPEN: the session changed main.rs (an import now prints unresolvable node references) but changed nothing about what it REALIZES, so every word above is still true.

⭐ WHAT MAKES IT WORTH RE-DATING RATHER THAN JUST NOT CLOSING: the session REPRODUCED the defect's cost without noticing at the time. All three of its ChangeEvents carried `affected` lists typed out from judgement — art:export, art:graph, art:main, art:schema-temporal, art:repair-notes-lifted-test, and later art:heal, art:service, art:tools-coherence — read off `reflow2_check.py`'s drift output rather than obtained from the graph. That is the identical workaround the 2026-08-06 entry describes, arrived at independently, by an agent that had not read this node.

🛑 SO THE HAND-NAMING IS NOT AN ANOMALY OF ONE SESSION; IT IS THE STANDING PRACTICE THIS DEFECT FORCES. The drift report names the FILES that changed, and mapping those to intent stays a human judgement — which is exactly the loop step this defect breaks. Two occurrences, 23 days apart, both silent, both only visible because someone looked.

The fix remains undecided (more REALIZES edges vs. finer artifact decomposition). What the second occurrence adds is evidence about COST: the workaround is cheap and reliable enough that nobody is forced to fix the cause, which is why it has survived 23 days.

═══ THIRD OCCURRENCE, 2026-08-29 (v0.43.0 CUT) — THE DEFECT CAUSED A FRESH UNDER-REGISTRATION HOURS AFTER A SESSION FIXED ONE ═══

Surfaced by `unclaimed_findings` again, the same single candidate via art:main, during the release cut. Left OPEN — every word above is still true — but this occurrence is a DIFFERENT and worse shape than the second, and it was made BY the session recording it.

WHAT HAPPENED: v0.43.0's headline fix (`cap:a-client-elects-a-server-of-its-own-build`) is served by TWO files. `crates/reflow2-mcp/src/shared.rs` decides — `exe_fingerprint()`, `should_reelect()`, the SIGTERM-and-respawn path. `crates/reflow2-mcp/src/main.rs:1104` PUBLISHES the fingerprint into the rendezvous, and without that half no client can ever match a build: the capability is not partially served without it, it is not served at all. Only `art:shared` was registered as realizing it. Verified by reading both files, not inferred.

⭐ THE PART THAT INDICTS THE SHAPE RATHER THAN THE AGENT: this same session had, an hour earlier, caught and repaired a MISSING REALIZES edge on this very capability (it had a passing check but no owning part and no file at all), was therefore actively thinking about exactly this class of omission, and STILL registered only one of the two files. Not from carelessness — from `art:main` being an atomic node whose name gives a session no reason to think of it as a participant in a shared-server capability. The registration a session reaches for is the file it edited MOST, and main.rs is nearly always the file it edited LEAST.

SO THE SECOND OCCURRENCE'S LESSON UNDERSTATES THIS. That entry says the defect forces a hand-naming WORKAROUND that is cheap and reliable. This one shows the workaround is NOT reliable: hand-naming from judgement is exactly what produced the under-registration, because judgement reaches for the file that felt like the change. The cost is no longer only a wrong blast radius on CLI changes — it is that new golden-thread edges get written INCOMPLETE, so the defect now propagates into the very traceability it corrupts.

WHAT WAS DONE ABOUT IT, AND WHAT WAS NOT: the missing `art:main REALIZES cap:a-client-elects-a-server-of-its-own-build` edge was drawn, because it records a true relationship and the release's headline capability should not ship with half a thread. 🛑 THAT EDGE DOES NOT REACH THE CAUSE and must not be read as a fix: it repairs ONE instance, by hand, using the same judgement that failed — which is the workaround, applied once more. The cause is `art:main`'s atomic granularity, the decision between more edges and finer decomposition is still open and still nobody's, and a fourth occurrence is the expected outcome of leaving it open.
